office.title: Indiana State Representative
office.summary: Members of the Indiana House of Representatives write and vote on state laws as part of the Indiana General Assembly. The House has 100 members, each representing one district for a two-year term [1].
duties: Introduces and votes on state legislation as one of the two chambers of the Indiana General Assembly [1].
Must be at least 21 years old when taking office and have lived in the district for at least a year [1].

incumbent.name: Wendy Dant Chesser
incumbent.summary: Wendy Dant Chesser of Jeffersonville, a former president and CEO of One Southern Indiana, was sworn in on June 4, 2024 after local Democrats chose her to finish Rep. Rita Fleming's term [3, 4]. She won a full term in November 2024 [5] and is seeking a second [6].
record: Committees: Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development; Financial Institutions; Insurance; and Roads and Transportation [3].

2025: Authored HEA 1226, the "Birthday Rule," which lets Medicare supplement (Medigap) enrollees switch plans without medical underwriting within 60 days of their birthday; it passed the House unanimously and the Senate 45-2 [7, 8]. Supported HB 1208, requiring quarterly reporting and training for sheriffs' jail commissary funds; in testimony she cited theft by former Clark County Sheriff Jamey Noel [7].

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) [9], and on the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) [10]; voted no on HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) [11]. Before that vote she said the proposed map was "completely unfair to residents of Southern Indiana" because it joined Jeffersonville with west-side Indianapolis [12].

Voted no on HB 1461 (2025), which allows new tolls on Indiana roads, saying "We cannot have more tolling in Southern Indiana" [7]. Voted no on HB 1343 (2026), citing a provision on a National Guard military police force the governor could deploy without local consent [12].

2026 bills she filed included a state-employer-parent child-care cost-sharing program, a pooled-benefits plan for child-care providers, a 3,520-foot buffer between vape or smoke shops and schools, and a first-time homebuyer savings program [12].

race_context: House District 71 covers Jeffersonville, Clarksville and part of New Albany, in Clark and Floyd counties [5, 3].

Not an open seat: Dant Chesser is the incumbent. She was chosen by a Democratic caucus in May 2024 after Rep. Rita Fleming retired immediately after the 2024 primary [13]. In November 2024 she defeated Republican Scott Hawkins and Libertarian Greg Hertzsch; in Clark County she received 49.4% to Hawkins' 46.7% [5].
May 5, 2026 Republican primary: James McClure Jr. 1,337 votes (55.1%), D.M. Bagshaw 1,090 (44.9%) [14]. Dant Chesser was unopposed in the Democratic primary [15, 14].
A Floyd County Republican Party debate before the primary included the Republican House District 71 candidates [16]. No general-election debate or forum for this race was found.

Key differences: Dant Chesser's campaign emphasizes jobs, child care, workforce training and government accountability [17]; in 2024 McClure listed repealing "red flag" laws, shrinking state government and parents' rights as priorities [18].

candidates.summary: James McClure Jr. is an Air Force and Navy veteran who has worked in information technology [18]. He lost the 2024 Republican primary for this seat and won the 2026 primary with 55.1% [19, 14].
background: In a 2024 LPM questionnaire he described himself as a veteran of the U.S. Air Force and U.S. Navy, including a 2005 deployment to Iraq, with 30 years in IT and more than 20 years of citizen activism [18].

Lists an associate degree from the Community College of the Air Force (1990), four years in the Air Force and five in the Navy Reserve, and Knights of Columbus membership [20]. Has previously sought a U.S. House seat [20].
path_to_ballot: Lost the 2024 Republican primary for District 71 to Scott Hawkins, 3,199 votes to 880 [19].
Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over D.M. Bagshaw, 1,337 votes (55.1%) to 1,090 [14].

items: In 2024 listed eliminating "red flag" laws and other state laws he considers unconstitutional as a priority [18].
In 2024 called for reducing the size and scope of state government by eliminating waste and redundancy to ease the tax burden [18].
In 2024 said he would protect parents' right to raise and educate their children as they see fit [18].

on_incumbent: No 2026 statements by McClure about Dant Chesser or her record were found.
plans: In 2024 said he would work with the next governor to "nullify federal overreach" and promised to serve a full term if elected [18].
endorsements_finance: iVoterGuide lists an endorsement he reported from state Sen. Chris Garten [20]. In 2024 he said he had accepted only local donations [18]. No 2026 fundraising totals were verified.
gaps: His positions above come from a 2024 questionnaire; no 2026 questionnaire answers, campaign website or news interviews were found.

Unverified (search snippets only): an Indiana Capital Chronicle voter guide says he previously ran in Democratic primaries for the 9th Congressional District in 2010, 2014 and 2016; lists his employer as Booth Veneer; and says his 2026 primary priorities were property taxes, eliminating fraud in state government and protecting liberty. iVoterGuide also lists a 2014 contribution from him to a Democratic Party organization.
What he said at the Floyd County Republican debate was not reported in the sources found.

candidates.summary: Wendy Dant Chesser is the incumbent, in office since June 2024 [3]. She led One Southern Indiana, the Clark-Floyd economic development group and chamber, for more than a decade [3].
background: Jeffersonville native; graduated from Jeffersonville High School and IU Southeast (business management); certified economic developer [3, 17].

Worked in the O'Bannon/Kernan administration and led the Indiana Rural Development Council; president and CEO of One Southern Indiana from 2012 [17, 3]. As of 2024 she was chief director of corporate strategy and external affairs at a regional employer [13].
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary [15, 14].

items: Authored the 2025 Medigap "Birthday Rule" law, saying it lowers seniors' risk of being denied coverage because of past claims or pre-existing conditions [8].

Says Indiana ranks 50th in licensed child-care facilities per capita and supports grants, tax credits and support for providers and parents [17]; filed 2026 bills to share child-care costs among the state, employers and parents [12].
Filed 2025 bills requiring ethics training for local elected officials and changing local campaign-finance reporting, and backed tighter jail commissary fund reporting [7].
Opposed allowing more tolling, saying people cross the Ohio River bridges often to work or go to school [7].
Opposed the 2025 congressional map, saying Southern Indiana is "impacted more by Louisville than by Indianapolis" [12]; voted no on HB 1032 [11].
Her campaign says she will keep fighting for the region's share of the state budget and for higher-paying jobs [17].

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by Dant Chesser about McClure were found.
plans: Campaign priorities: transparency and accountability, jobs, education and workforce development, and affordable child care [17].
endorsements_finance: iVoterGuide lists endorsements from the AFL-CIO, the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee, Better Indiana, Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and the Indiana House Democratic Caucus [21]. No 2026 fundraising totals were verified.
gaps: No public statement by her on the Meta data center being built in Jeffersonville was found.
Her yes votes on SEA 1 and the 2025 budget are from roll calls; no statements explaining those votes were found.
No campaign finance reports were reviewed.
